# kiwix-tools

**Kiwix's command-line reader, server and library manager for offline ZIM books**

- **Version recorded:** 3.7.0
- **Categories:** `references`
- **Upstream:** <https://github.com/kiwix/kiwix-tools>

## What it does

Reads ZIM files, the single-file offline copies of Wikipedia, Stack Exchange sites, WikiMed and hundreds of other books that the Kiwix project publishes. `kiwix-serve` serves them as web pages with full-text search, `kiwix-search` searches one from a terminal, and `kiwix-manage` keeps the library file that lists them.

## Why you would want it

With the network down, an encyclopaedia, a medical reference and the whole of Amateur Radio Stack Exchange are still on the laptop and searchable. It is the reader for the books `kiwix-library` installs, and for any ZIM you bring yourself. The alternative is the `kiwix` desktop reader, which is heavier and needs a desktop session; this runs anywhere, including over SSH to a Pi.

## Before it will work

Books to read: choose them with `hammunition station set --reference-books`, or bring your own ZIM file. Nothing else.

## How it installs

- apt: `kiwix-tools`

## Known problems

kiwix-serve listens on every network address of the machine unless told otherwise, and its default port, 80, needs root (both measured 2026-09-29). Run it through `hammunition reference serve`, which always passes `-i 127.0.0.1` and a high port; if you run it by hand, pass `-i 127.0.0.1 -p 8481` yourself, or anyone on the network can read your library. Debian's libzim (9.2.3) is several releases behind upstream and reads the format-6.3 ZIMs Kiwix publishes today. The package pulls aria2 as a dependency of libkiwix; nothing here uses it.
